messages:
Sofia: Hi all, quick onboarding benefit questions. I enrolled in medical but missed vision during the initial form. Is vision separate or part of the medical bundle? Also wondering when HSA eligibility kicks in and if I can contribute mid-year.
Sofia: Also my offer included a "home office" monthly reimbursement for 3 months. Is that processed through payroll or expense?
benefits-bot: Welcome to Redwood! Helpful docs: benefits portal https://benefits.redwood.example, HSA FAQ https://benefits.redwood.example/hsa, expense portal https://expenses.redwood.example.
Maya (People Ops): Hey Sofia, congrats and welcome. Vision is a separate optional election; it's not auto-enrolled with medical. If you're within 30 days of your hire date you can add it now and coverage will begin the 1st of the month after enrollment processes.
Maya (People Ops): HSA: if you enrolled in the HSA-eligible medical plan you're eligible to start contributions as soon as your medical election is active. Elections made during initial enrollment are effective the 1st of next month; you can change contributions during open enrollment or after a qualifying life event. Employer contributions (if any) will be scheduled per the contributions plan in Workday.
Lina (Payroll): Home office stipend: we handle recurring stipends via payroll if the offer says "monthly stipend." For a 3-month monthly reimbursement we need a record in Workday payroll allowances. If it's a one-time reimbursement you'd use Expensify. Can you paste the exact stipend wording from your offer?
Sofia: Offer line: "Home office reimbursement: $75/month for 3 months, paid as a monthly stipend."
Lina (Payroll): Thanks — that reads as a payroll stipend. I'll coordinate with HR to add the allowance so it shows up on the next payroll cycle after we enter it. Expect it to appear as a separate line on your paystub.
Sofia: Great, thanks. For vision, if I add it now will there be any backdating to cover today's optometrist appointment?
Maya (People Ops): Coverage can't be backdated. If you need immediate coverage because of an appointment, you can use the paid claim and submit receipts, but benefits won't retroactively cover pre-enrollment visits.
Sofia: Understood. One last thing: is PTO accrued from day one or do we get an initial bank?
Maya (People Ops): PTO accrual starts on your hire date and accrues biweekly based on your policy and FTE. New hires do not get a lump-sum except for company observed holidays which are granted to everyone. See PTO policy: https://handbook.redwood.example/pto.
Sofia: Perfect, thank you all! I'll add vision in the portal now and ping if any issues.
Maya (People Ops): Ping us if you want help doing it live. Welcome aboard :tada:
